verdict.detail: No action needed from Georg right now, and that is the recommendation: all four of his bids are live at the right numbers and the first of them resolves within the hour. Do not raise, do not remove, do not sell before they land. The one thing that changed this run is news, not market: the Club Bruegge interest in Sylla is now corroborated by Schalke-region reporting published minutes before this run, which flips the previous run's premise that the story was uncorroborated. Sell Sylla the moment the squad count makes it legal, and do not wait for the German window to shut.

sell.reason: Sylla is the live one and the urgency went up this run. Schalke-region reporting dated today names Club Bruegge, says talks over an immediate transfer have been held, and says the Schalke board is weighing whether to let him go before the window closes; the club's valuation line and the extended Turkish and Saudi windows both still stand, so the exit risk does not expire with the German deadline and runs through the matchday lock. He is fit and started, so this is a transfer-risk sale, not a fitness one. Sell as soon as the count makes it legal and no sooner: with a full complement the sale leaves a legal five-three-two, but if the second defender lands and the midfield body does not, the sale is illegal and must not be attempted. Behind Sylla the funding queue is unchanged: Widmer first once the squad is comfortably legal, since he sits outside the best eleven either way and is bleeding value daily, then Bernardo only if his non-fit flag is still showing near the lock. Lokonga stays a quality sale rather than an availability one, and he must never be sold in the same move as Sylla.

buy.reason: Nothing new is worth buying, which makes four runs in a row. The board added four manager asks, three of them defenders in a position that is already covered and capped, and the fourth a midfielder whose points-per-euro is roughly three times worse than the defender already bid for. Two of the four are priced at exactly market value, which looks like the low-cluster bargain the ledger says to take on a manager ask — it is not, because that rule says what to pay for a player worth having, not that every ask at market value is worth having. One of the defenders is the same player a previous run lost at auction, now being flipped by the winner at a small gross margin, and at the new ask his value is materially worse than the benchmark the ledger recorded for him. One more is a name-recognition trap: a long-established starter with no minutes at all this season, which is the more important fact than the modest price. Two earlier avoid calls have left the board unactioned, correctly. The live bids stand as they are: hold the defender bid rather than raising it, since it already sits at the top of the measured mid-price contested band; hold the midfield bid, which is already above the recommendation and correctly inside the cheap-listing high cluster; and leave the cheap Elversberg option alone until the midfield body resolves, at which point the recount decides whether to remove it or raise it into the high cluster.

movers.reason: No flip clears its cost this run. There are no manager asks below market value at all, so the mechanism the ledger measures is simply absent. What the rivals are doing instead is not a model to copy: three same-day round trips completed this run, all sold back at exactly market value for gross margins in the low tens of thousands on seven-figure outlays, and one of the three players involved has a torn knee ligament and is out for weeks. That is motion, not points, and it consumes a squad slot Georg cannot spare while he is short of a legal eleven. One useful mechanic did fall out of it, worth keeping: every sale back to the market in this feed cleared at exactly market value, so a sale price can be read as the market value without spending a lookup call.

fitness.sweep: Clean sweep. The injured-and-suspended table dated today lists none of the squad and none of the four bid targets, and none of the four new listings either. Bernardo still carries a non-fit flag on his Kickbase listing with nothing behind it on the injury table, so the reading is unchanged: the flag looks like the early substitution for his direct competitor rather than an injury. Note that a clean flag is not proof of fitness in the other direction — several cheap listings on the board carry clean flags only because the player has never been in a matchday squad to be flagged, and the ledger has three of those logged as traps.
